response.sql: WITH s AS (SELECT c.State AS State, SUM(i.Total) AS state_total, COUNT(*) AS invoice_count FROM Invoice i JOIN Customer c ON c.CustomerId = i.CustomerId WHERE i.InvoiceDate > '2010-06-22 00:00:00' AND i.InvoiceDate < '2012-06-26 00:00:00' GROUP BY c.State) SELECT SUM(state_total) AS total_sum, AVG(invoice_count) AS avg_invoices_per_state FROM s

assumptions.assumption: The request says 'per customer State' with the NULL-state customers forming one group. GROUP BY puts NULLs together, so that group counts as one state in the average.
InvoiceDate is compared as text with plain string comparison against the given bounds. Both bounds are exclusive.
The average is the mean of the per-state invoice counts. AVG over integer counts is not rounded in SQLite. In engines that use integer division, a cast to a decimal type may be needed.
